newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 2-yr, 5-yr fixed bond prices seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Polish 2-yr, 5-yr fixed bond prices seen falling.

text.p: Prices of Poland's 16-percent two-year and 12-percent five-year fixed bonds are expected to fall at Thursday's joint 700 million zloty primary tender, analysts said on Wednesday.

They said investors are likely to test higher yields mainly because year-on-year inflation did not decline in October as expected, but remained flat at 19.5 percent, which could make players willing to gamble for lower prices.
"Inflation was higher than expected, so investors may bid for higher yields at Thursday's tender," said Piotr Dalkowski, analyst at Pioneer fund in Warsaw.

The rapid 1.8 percent rise in food prices in the first 10 days of November, up from a 0.1 percent increase in the previous 10 days, added to the market's uncertainty about the level of year-on-year inflation at the 1996 end.
The government had said year-on-year CPI would fall between 17.9 and 18.2 percent in December, while market analysts see 1996 price growth at around 18.7 percent.

Analysts said the demand should not top the finance ministry's 700 million zloty offer with the focus remaining on the shorter two-year bonds, which seem to be attractive even in an environment of rising T-bill yields.
They said investors should bid for around 500 million zlotys of the shorter paper and between 100 and 200 million of the longer bonds.

Analysts expected yields for the two-year paper, maturing February 12, 1999, to inch up toward secondary market levels of 20.2 to 20.3 percent on Thursday from 20.08 percent at the last fixed bond auction on October 17.
"The two-year paper now gives a yield of 70 basis points over the 52-week T-bill, which makes it attractive," an analyst at investment company said.
The average yield of the five-year paper, maturing in February 12, 2002, was expected to rise by about 0.1 point from 18.10 percent at the last primary auction.
The settlement date of the shorter paper is December 5, 1996 and December 12, 1996 for the longer bond.
